review_notes:
I reviewed the whole file, which contains one theorem, `NoncollapsedRCD.regular_good_coordinate_sets`, on lines 17–55. I read the two lemmas it relies on, `NoncollapsedRCD.full_splitting_coordinates` and `NoncollapsedRCD.regular_large_good_sets`. I also read `FirstOrderSplittingOn.mono_error`, where `μ` and `hQ` are explicit section variables, which is why the call uses `_ _`. I compared the file with its sibling `regular_good_coordinate_sets_bounded`. That sibling has to state `t ≤ β`, so its `min` on `t` is needed; the `min ε 1` in this file is not.

There are two findings. The main one is that the tolerance `t := min ε 1` is unnecessary. The second, smaller one is that the bounds hidden in `S` can be unpacked more clearly with `lt_min_iff`; I confirmed that lemma exists in Mathlib (`Mathlib/Order/Defs/LinearOrder.lean`).

I left the `hcurv` argument (lines 50–53) as it is. It is a clear, explicit bound using `abs`, and the obvious shorter version would be a single, harder-to-read `nlinarith` call. I could not compile anything, so none of the replacements below have been checked by Lean.

findings.excerpt:
let t := min ε 1
  have ht : 0 < t := lt_min he zero_lt_one
  have htε : t ≤ ε := min_le_left _ _
findings.problem: The proof sets the splitting tolerance to `t := min ε 1`. The cap at 1 is never used. The only facts about `t` the proof needs are `0 < t` (to call `regular_large_good_sets`) and `t ≤ ε` (to feed `hcoord`). The theorem statement only promises `∃ t, 0 < t ∧ ...`, with no upper bound on `t`. Because of the cap, the proof needs `ht`, `htε`, and an extra `.mono_error _ _ ht.le htε` step at the end, just to raise the tolerance back up to `ε`.
findings.proposed_change:
Use `ε` directly as the tolerance:
```lean
  obtain ⟨ε,he,hcoord⟩ := hX.full_splitting_coordinates hn hpublished hη
  obtain ⟨s,hs,hgood⟩ := hX.regular_large_good_sets hn hp he hζ
  let S := min s (min 1 (ε/(|K|+1)))
  have hS : 0 < S := lt_min hs (lt_min zero_lt_one (by positivity))
  refine ⟨ε,S,he,hS,?_⟩
  ... -- unchanged
  exact hcoord x r hr hcurv u v
    (hall x hx (16*r) (by positivity) (by linarith only [hrR]))
```
This deletes lines 30–32 and the `.mono_error _ _ ht.le htε` call. `hall` then directly gives `FirstOrderSplittingOn … x (16*r) ε u v`, which is the hypothesis `hcoord` expects.
findings.benefit: The proof gets shorter, and the reader no longer has to ask why the tolerance is capped at 1 when nothing uses that. The key idea becomes easier to see: the good sets are built at exactly the tolerance `ε` that the coordinate theorem needs, and the result is passed straight through without a monotonicity detour.

FirstOrderSplittingOn (hausdorff n X) hX.quadratic x r t u v := by
(h : FirstOrderSplittingOn μ hQ p r ε u v) (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hεδ : ε ≤ δ) :

findings.excerpt:
have hR1 : R ≤ 1 := (hRS.le.trans (min_le_right _ _)).trans (min_le_left _ _)
  have hRe : R ≤ ε/(|K|+1) :=
    (hRS.le.trans (min_le_right _ _)).trans (min_le_right _ _)
findings.problem: The three bounds hidden in `S = min s (min 1 (ε/(|K|+1)))` are recovered with hand-built chains of `min_le_left`/`min_le_right`. To see which bound each chain produces, the reader has to follow the `left`/`right` path through the nested `min`. Two of the three are also weakened from `<` to `≤` along the way. Separately, the step after them uses `nlinarith`, even though the goal follows linearly from `R*(|K|+1) ≤ ε` and `0 < R`.
findings.proposed_change:
Unpack the `min` with the named Mathlib lemma `lt_min_iff`:
```lean
  obtain ⟨hRs, hR1e⟩ := lt_min_iff.mp hRS
  obtain ⟨hR1, hRe⟩ := lt_min_iff.mp hR1e
  have hKR : |K| * R ≤ ε := by
    have hh := (lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity : 0 < |K|+1)).mp hRe
    linarith only [hh,hR]
```
This makes `hR1 : R < 1` and `hRe : R < ε/(|K|+1)` strict. The later `nlinarith only [hrR',hr,hR1,hR]` still works, because a strict hypothesis is stronger than the `≤` version.
findings.benefit: Each bound now comes from destructuring with a well-named lemma, so the reader sees directly that `R < S` splits into `R < s`, `R < 1` and `R < ε/(|K|+1)`. This replaces three different `trans` chains. Using `linarith` also makes clear that the `|K|*R ≤ ε` step is only linear rearrangement.

evidence.excerpt: lemma lt_min (h₁ : a < b) (h₂ : a < c) : a < min b c := lt_min_iff.mpr ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
